newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Stocks on Cyprus exchange down in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Stocks on Cyprus exchange down in thin trade.

text.p: Cyprus stocks edged lower by 0.49 percent in shallow trading at week end Friday with losses registered in six of seven sub-indices.
The Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) 41-share general index closed at 77.73 points on Friday after closing at 78.12 on May 2.

CISCO, the Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation, said in its weekly report the market lost ground on Monday because of the technical adjustment in the share price of Hellenic Bank for the payment of the 1996 dividend of 15 cents per share.
Shares in national carrier Cyprus Airways were trading at 28.4 cents on Friday, marking a rise from 27.7 cents last week.

The airline was shaken by a wave of bad publicity this week after disclosure that a pilot enforcing a union work-to-rule directive landed a plane full of foreign tourists at the wrong airport. Flying the plane to its proper destination would have meant working 10 minutes overtime.

The incident prompted a warning from the finance minister that the government could withhold its guarantee for a $30 million loan the company was seeking for aircraft maintenance and to renew an existing short-term loan.
Pilots have since suspended their measures, adopted in protest at work being transferred to Eurocypria, the Cyprus Airways charter subsidiary.

Banking stocks closed at 86.64, down 0.64 percent, or 0.56 points from last week. Bank of Cyprus shares closed at 311, 13.5 cents lower, while the Cyprus Popular Bank closed at 303, down half a cent from last week.
Shares of Hellenic Bank were trading at 277.5 on Friday from 291.5 last week. Universal Savings Bank closed at 188, from 192.5 last week.
The insurance index was 1.17 percent lower, closing on Friday at 58.70 points.

The mid-price for Universal Life shares was 433.5 on Friday, down 26.5 cents from last week. Interamerican, the insurance company specialising in life insurance, announced an 81 percent pre-tax profit jump in 1996 over the previous year. Last year the company acquired the life portfolios of holding company Paneuropean and associate company Philiki.

It closed at 99 cents on Friday from 96.5 last week. Paneuropean, which announced cosolidated pre-tax profits of 2.4 million pounds in 1996, was trading at 107.5, up three cents on last week's closing price.
Philiki shares closed at 261, down half a cent from last week. It announced consolidated group profits of 4.6 million pounds.
Keo, the Cyprus beer and wine company, was trading at 103, half a cent lower.
Vassiliko Cement shares were trading unchanged at 167.5.
